title: Micro-shift longlink failover: SLO-driven per-connection traffic ramp and graceful egress
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Hosted API customers maintain many long-lived connections (websockets, chunked streaming). Existing region-level cutovers are coarse and either force-closes connections or cause token/continuity mismatches. We need a failover strategy that preserves in-progress streams, meets customer-facing latency SLOs, and avoids throttling spikes during multi-region incidents.

Proposal (Micro-shift Longlink Failover): Introduce a per-connection micro-shift controller that performs staggered, SLO-governed traffic transfers for long-lived connections. Instead of draining by region, we migrate connections at connection granularity with lightweight checkpoints and a telemetry-driven ramp. Key features: 
- Per-connection transfer windows (micro-epochs): small, time-boxed handoffs where a subset of active connections are migrated to a target region or replica.
- Soft-proxy token stitching: ephemeral edge proxies generate short-lived continuity tokens allowing the destination to resume KV-cache-backed decode state for streaming generators where possible.
- SLO-governed ramp: telemetry (p99 latency, token generation rate, worker headroom) drives the percentage of connections shifted per micro-epoch. Ramp-up is throttled when SLOs are near violation.
- Connection priority tiers: interactive requests (low-latency chat sessions) get higher transfer priority than background embeddings or batch inference; lower tiers can be shed early.
- Circuit-breaker integration: region-level and per-worker CBs expose hysteresis gates to the micro-shift controller. If destination circuits open, controller pauses migration and falls back to hedging or local serve.
- Graceful fallback: if stitch fails, controller will attempt a transparent fallback to a compatible model variant in the origin region, with clear error metrics surfaced to users.

Why unique: current strategies in the repo are either whole-region drains or per-request hedging. This approach targets sustaining longlink continuity while bounding the cost/risk of mass cutovers and preserving token/KV coherence for streaming outputs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Automated micro-shift controller can move 5-10% of live longlinks per micro-epoch without increasing p99 latency beyond configured headroom.
2) Streaming continuity tokens can rehydrate KV-cache for >=70% of migratable generator sessions in lab tests.
3) Circuit-breaker signals cause immediate pause of migration and automatic local fallback.
4) Rollback path returns all migrated connections to origin if error budget burn rate exceeds threshold within 10 minutes.
5) Playbook and runbook validated in staging and exercised once in chaos window.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 - Design (Week 1-2): finalize token format, checkpoint payload (small, e.g., last KV pointers + minimal meta), CB integration points, and SLO telemetry thresholds. Deliverable: design doc in Confluence (link below).
Phase 2 - Control plane: implement micro-shift controller service with API to query connection lists, prioritize, and issue transfer commands. Add feature flags and safety toggles.
Phase 3 - Edge agent changes: minimal proxy to accept continuity tokens and attempt rehydrate; fallback to hedged routing if rehydrate not possible.
Phase 4 - Observability: new metrics (migrated_connections_count, migrate_success_rate, migrate_latency_p99, stitch_rehydrate_rate, rollback_count, sloa_burn_during_migration). Add dashboards and SLO alerts.
Phase 5 - Staged rollout: internal canary -> regional staging -> global with SLO-governed ramping.
Phase 6 - Postmortem & tuning: collect data, tune micro-epoch size and priority weights.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Micro-Shift+Longlink+Failover
- Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1127
- Spec for continuity token: https://drive.google.com/file/dummy-token-spec
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated - disabled by default.
2) Internal dev canary: enable for 1% of internal traffic for 24h, verify metrics.
3) Staging: enable for all staging regions with synthetic traffic (10k streams) and chaos tests (region outage simulation).
4) Gradual production ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% with 2-hour observation windows, only advancing when p99 latency headroom and error budget thresholds satisfied.
5) Emergency cutoff: toggle to stop migrations immediately; automated rollback if additive SLO burn in last 10 minutes > 20% of SLO window.
6) Finalize GA after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and runbook signoff.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for token generation and validation.
- Integration tests: origin proxy issues token -> destination attempts stitch -> continue streaming. Use deterministic seed models to validate byte-continuity.
- Load test: simulate 50k concurrent longlinks, measure migrate_success_rate and p99 tail.
- Chaos tests: simulate destination region partial outage and verify controller pauses and triggers fallback.
- Regression tests: ensure existing short-lived requests unaffected and cost telemetry remains stable.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Metrics to create: migrated_connections_count (gauge), migration_attempt_rate (counter), migration_success_rate (ratio), stitch_rehydrate_rate (ratio), migration_latency_ms_p50_p95_p99, migration_rollback_count (counter), sloa_burn_rate_during_migration (gauge).
Alerts: P0 alert if migration_success_rate < 80% for >5m during ramp.
SLO gates enforced by controller: if sloa_burn_rate_during_migration > configured threshold -> immediate pause and incremental rollback.
Dashboards: per-region migration health, per-priority-tier breakdown, and correlated worker headroom heatmap.
security_review_notes: KMS usage required for continuity token signing. Token lifetime strictly limited (TTL default 60s). Security requested a threat model review - link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Micro-Shift+Threat+Model. Need to add HSM KMS integration for GA.
notes_and_decisions:
- Decision 2026-02-25: use signed opaque continuity tokens instead of replay-able checkpoints to reduce data leakage risk.
- Trade-off: full KV sync is expensive; we checkpoint only recent KV pointers and fall back to re-generation when necessary.
- Decision 2026-03-03: micro-epoch size set to 2% of active longlinks by default; adjustable per-region.
- Follow-up: evaluate adaptive micro-epoch sizing based on predictive load for Q3.
